subject.title: [Bug]: browser navigation-guard explicit hostname allowlist broken by SSRF loopback tightening (#100835)

question: Should browser navigation exact-host allowlist entries continue to allow non-localhost hostnames that resolve to loopback after the trusted-host SSRF tightening?
rationale: Both outcomes are plausible security/product choices: preserving the old test restores an operator-declared browser exception, while retiring it keeps the newly accepted loopback-rebinding hardening intact.

options.title: Retire old loopback-alias contract
options.body: Keep the hardened trusted-host loopback behavior and update the browser navigation contract to require explicit localhost, loopback literals, or deliberate private-network opt-in.

options.title: Approve scoped browser exception
options.body: Allow only the maintainer-approved loopback case for browser navigation allowlists while preserving metadata and link-local DNS-answer blocking.

options.title: Defer to wider SSRF design
options.body: Keep the issue and linked PR blocked until the browser SSRF allowlist model is decided with related private-network confirmation work.

recommendation.title: Retire old loopback-alias contract
recommendation.body: Keep the hardened trusted-host loopback behavior and update the browser navigation contract to require explicit localhost, loopback literals, or deliberate private-network opt-in.

likelyOwner.reason: They opened this issue and provided the clearest recent maintainer acceptance signal on the SSRF loopback hardening boundary.
